name: A Sewanee woods lot

place_source.title: Wikidata: Sewanee (Q1987614), coordinate location and elevation above sea level

blurb: A wooded lot on the Cumberland Plateau near Sewanee, Tennessee: mature oak-hickory forest with a scattered understory of dogwood, sourwood, and evergreen holly, visited by white-tailed deer, wild turkeys, and a chorus of woodland birds.

facts.text: Sewanee sits on the Cumberland Plateau at about 588 m elevation, with a humid subtropical climate (Köppen Cfa).

source.title: Wikipedia: Sewanee, Tennessee
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Sewanee, Tennessee", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The plateau's forests are dominated by oak-hickory associations, with white oak, northern red oak, shagbark hickory, and pignut hickory as canopy trees.

source.title: Wikipedia: Cumberland Plateau
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Cumberland Plateau", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: White-tailed deer are abundant on the Cumberland Plateau and are a key herbivore shaping forest understory composition.

source.title: Wikipedia: White-tailed deer
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "White-tailed deer", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The pileated woodpecker excavates large nest cavities in dead trees that are later used by many other species including owls, bats, and flying squirrels.

source.title: Wikipedia: Pileated woodpecker
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Pileated woodpecker", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The eastern box turtle is Tennessee's state reptile and can live over 50 years in the wild, but road mortality and habitat loss threaten local populations.

source.title: Wikipedia: Common box turtle
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Common box turtle", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
